prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / fantasy cartography.
Create a beautiful, carefully readable TOP-DOWN WORLD OF WARCRAFT-STYLE ZONE MAP for Ashveil's starting chapter, an ORIGINAL geography and original artwork. This is a practical level-design reference following an authored story. Landscape 3:2 composition, high-resolution, preferably 3072x2048. The world map fills the sheet; reserve a narrow parchment legend strip at the bottom. Strict top-down cartographic view: no horizon, no oblique panorama, no isometric scene. Hand-painted parchment, softly colored forest canopy clusters, roof-footprint village symbols, fine ink contour hatching on cream limestone ridges, olive-green fields, ochre paths, muted blue river, legible dark serif place labels with discreet parchment halos. Classic richly illustrated MMO zone-map feeling, restrained border and small compass rose, not a modern GPS map or a flowchart. Large landforms and readable paths first, small texture second.

TITLE: "ALDERBANK & THE LOWER ROAD".
Small subtitle: "Chapter One · A Fire Worth Keeping".

GEOGRAPHY / POSITION CONTRACT, NORTH AT TOP:
The River Alder runs north-to-south through the LEFT THIRD of the page, a natural gently bending river. The living safe bank is EAST / RIGHT of it, occupying most of the map. All playable locations and ALL main-story roads are on this same EAST bank. Across the river on the WEST / LEFT is Bracken Hollow: a modest old village and countryside fading into silent grey desaturation. No fire, lava, smoke wall, floating ash particles or evil fortress. Bracken is contextual and inaccessible in this chapter; no quest route crosses the river.

Arrange EAST-bank landmarks as this connected network (percentages refer to map area above the bottom legend):
- "Alderbank Refuge" near (57%,25%): warm tiny terracotta-roofed village around a communal yard/fire, a store shed and small fenced practice yard. It is a HOME HUB, not a castle or city.
- "Safe Landing" directly west of the refuge beside the east riverbank (41%,27%): shingle, reeds, small ferry jetty, willow shelf. A small failed rope-footbridge/ferry site here suggests the opening escape; no intact crossing.
- "Westmere Farm" east and slightly south of refuge (84%,29%): cottage, barn, lived-in field strips, irrigation headgate and small channel footbridge. Optional loop from refuge east to farm, then south-west to the wagon.
- "Stranded Wagon" southeast of refuge (70%,48%): one overturned covered wagon beside a broad road, small meadow and farm fields. Caption nearby "Wagon Road & Fields". The main road leaves refuge southeast to this site.
- "Old Orchard" southeast of wagon (85%,61%): clearly ordered fruit-tree canopies, tiny beehive boxes at its east edge, a clearing. A small road-loop spur also reaches the orchard.
- "Alder Grove" southwest of orchard (73%,78%): a dense but welcoming alder stand. An optional trail joins orchard to grove and then turns west-northwest toward the rally.
- "Lower Road" is the broad winding corridor from wagon southwest toward (52%,69%); label the ROAD along its length. Include a few inconspicuous pale ward stones.
- "Waystation Rally" at (48%,73%), WEST-NORTHWEST of grove: a small sheltered landing/camp, then a broad traversable descent southwest.
- "Broken Waystation" at (42%,88%), southwest of the rally: small cream-stone ruin with a dungeon-entry arch embedded below the EAST-bank abutment of an OLD BROKEN STONE CROSSING. The station is EAST/right/inland of its bridge abutment. Broad path from rally reaches entry WITHOUT crossing water. Show a clearly MISSING bridge span over the river: the two damaged ends never connect. This old crossing is separate from the small failed ferry/rope site near the refuge.
- A faint road/sign leads NORTH from refuge and stops at the map boundary. Tiny label "North Road · future lead"; no destination or new region drawn.

ROUTE OVERLAY, sparse and precise:
Thin gold main-story trail with small numbered pins: 1 at Safe Landing/refuge opening, 2 at wagon, 3 at rally, 4 at dungeon entrance, 5 in the refuge communal yard (homecoming). Gold road connects 1->2->3->4. An understated gold dashed return line with occasional northbound arrowheads follows THE SAME ROAD BACK from waystation through rally and wagon to refuge; label it once "Return to Alderbank". It does not shortcut over river or through optional orchard/farm loops.
Optional loops use thin dashed TEAL paths: refuge-farm-wagon; wagon-orchard-grove-rally. Side content NEVER blocks the gold route. Put tiny readable teal tags near the regions: "S01-S05" at refuge, "S06-S10" spanning wagon/fields/orchard-edge, "S11-S13" at farm, "S14-S16" at orchard, "S17-S18" on lower-road approach, "S19-S20" beside dungeon entrance. Grove itself is only an optional exploration label, NOT assigned S14-S16.
Only a dungeon entrance icon, NO dungeon floorplan or underground cutaway.

BOTTOM LEGEND, crisply readable and compact:
Gold line: "Main story" ; teal dashed line: "Optional side stories".
"1  Rescue, care & first weapon · M01-M03"
"2  Secure the wagon · M04-M05"
"3  Scout the Lower Road & wards · M06-M07"
"4  Rescue the missing · M08"
"5  Reunion & the next lead · M09-M10"
Small footer: "Chapter layout study · Not to scale".
Use a tasteful two-column legend arrangement. Labels must not obscure junctions or terrain. Preserve generous breathing room. No game logo, giant UI panels, chat windows, minimap, player characters, level numbers, coordinates, invented place names or extra quest stages. This should be a compelling classic fantasy zone map that a level designer can use to understand geography, optional travel, escalation and the return-home story arc.
corrections: Edit this Ashveil illustrated zone map with THREE precise connectivity corrections, preserving its composition, art style, colors, all place names, all numbered pins, side-quest tags, compass, bottom legend and typography. 1) The dashed gold trail labeled 'Return to Alderbank' currently makes an inland shortcut between the Waystation Rally and Alderbank Refuge, skipping the Stranded Wagon. REMOVE that shortcut trail and its independent dirt-road branch, restore continuous meadow/trees there. Redraw the gold return dashes IMMEDIATELY ALONGSIDE the existing SOLID GOLD main road, traversing exactly pin 4 Broken Waystation -> pin 3 Waystation Rally -> pin 2 Stranded Wagon -> pin 5 Alderbank Refuge. Return arrowheads point toward Alderbank. It must go through the wagon junction; no shortcut. Move the 'Return to Alderbank' label to this same road. 2) At the old BROKEN STONE bridge beside Broken Waystation in the lower-left, remove the dangling ropes/posts/planks spanning between the two stone remnants. There must be a large obvious uninterrupted BLUE WATER GAP between the stone bridge stubs, absolutely no rope or walkway connecting the banks. Preserve both ruined abutments and the east-bank waystation entrance. 3) Make the dashed teal optional farm loop visibly CONNECT from Alderbank Refuge to Westmere Farm and then to the STRANDED WAGON road junction. Do not let it terminate in the trees north of the wagon. Preserve all other optional trails. Do not add any new labels or landmarks, do not relocate any settlement, do not change the top-down map framing. Keep text sharp and readable.

Make ONLY these two small finishing edits to this map. Preserve every other pixel/composition, all geography, all gold roads and return arrows, bridge water gap, place names, side-quest badges, bottom legend and border. First: under the 'Broken Waystation' label at lower-left, REPLACE the subtitle 'Old stones. Unfinished business.' with the exact text 'Service entrance below · M08'. Keep its S19-S20 badge below it and keep the entrance arch visible. Second: simplify and finish the optional TEAL FARM ROUTE so it is ONE clearly continuous path linking Alderbank Refuge -> Westmere Farm -> Stranded Wagon junction (pin 2). Remove the extra teal arc looping north above the farm. From the farm's channel bridge, guide the teal dashes southwest along the existing dirt farm track to touch the actual wagon-road junction by pin 2, not stop in the trees or at the place label. It may pass discreetly behind labels but must have visible connected endpoints. Leave the orchard/grove teal routes exactly as they are. Do not change anything else. Keep typography crisp.

visualResearch.role: Classic WoW zone-map visual research via image search: parchment, terrain drawing, road network and readable place labels; no external image supplied to generation.
Viewed for Ashveil palette and living-versus-desaturated contrast only. Its compressed perspective/layout was not used as a map or supplied as a generation reference.

layoutDecisions: Concept map orientation is north=+world z, east=-world x. The runtime does not define a compass; this presentation preserves its landmark topology while honoring the script's east-road escape and east-verge wagon.
River Alder is west/left of the playable safe bank, Bracken Hollow is across it to the west. All required playable roads and dungeon entrance stay on the east bank.

Separate small failed ferry/rope site near refuge and old broken stone crossing above the waystation are a provisional interpretation of two authored crossing beats, not a newly settled geography contract.
Detailed S14-S16 scripts place Nella's chain at Old Orchard/bee row; Alder Grove is shown as optional exploration despite the chapter bundle's shorthand grove outing.

Numbered pins summarize chapter regions and story beats, not every turn-in or a single uninterrupted outing. M04/M05 return to Alderbank before M06/M07; the shared gold corridor also supports that return. Optional stories may revisit the refuge.
No dungeon interior, next-region destination, exact scale, collision topology or production-level layout is specified by the illustration.
status: Illustrated chapter planning reference, not runtime integration or evidence that all chapter content is playable.
